source: European Food Safety Authority (EFSA), topic pages read 13 September 2026. EFSA does not classify teratogens; it derives health-based guidance values for substances in the food chain. The values below are quoted as EFSA states them.
note: OpenFoodTox 3.0, EFSA's structured hazard database (7,880 substances, 19,452 reference values, April 2026), is the machine-readable route to the rest. Its host was unreachable on 13 September 2026, so this file carries the values read from EFSA's own pages; tools/enrich-teratogens-efsa.py attaches them and will take the database when it answers again.

values.label: Methylmercury
values.value: Tolerable weekly intake 1.3 µg per kg of body weight, expressed as mercury
values.note: EFSA states that its tolerable weekly intake of 1.3 μg/kg body weight for methylmercury remains valid, while noting that an updated assessment may be appropriate.

values.label: Inorganic mercury
values.value: Tolerable weekly intake 4 µg per kg of body weight, expressed as mercury
values.note: Established by EFSA in 2012; in June 2026 EFSA reviewed the United States toxicological profile of 2024 and concluded that the value remains valid.

values.label: Cadmium
values.value: Tolerable weekly intake 2.5 µg per kg of body weight
values.note: Established in 2009; EFSA reassessed it in February 2011 after the Joint FAO/WHO Expert Committee on Food Additives reviewed cadmium, and concluded it is still appropriate.

values.label: Dioxins and dioxin-like PCBs
values.value: Tolerable weekly intake 0.6 pg per kg of body weight, for the group
values.note: Set by EFSA in its 2018 risk assessment for combined exposure to dioxins and dioxin-like polychlorinated biphenyls, using toxic equivalency factors.

values.label: Nickel
values.value: Tolerable daily intake 13 µg per kg of body weight
values.note: EFSA updated its advice on nickel in food and drinking water in October 2020 and raised the tolerable daily intake from 2.8 to 13 µg/kg of body weight.

values.label: Bisphenol A
values.value: Tolerable daily intake cut in April 2023; banned in food contact materials since December 2024
values.note: EFSA re-evaluated bisphenol A in April 2023 and significantly reduced the tolerable daily intake it had set in 2015, which was 4 µg per kg of body weight per day. Taking that assessment into account, the European Commission adopted a ban on bisphenol A in food contact materials on 19 December 2024.

values.label: PFOA, PFOS, PFNA and PFHxS
values.value: Group tolerable weekly intake 4.4 ng per kg of body weight
values.note: EFSA set the group value for these four per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances in 2020. The critical effect is the decreased response of the immune system to vaccination; EFSA notes that exposure during pregnancy and breastfeeding is the main contributor to the levels found in infants.

values.label: DEHP, DBP, BBP and DINP
values.value: Group tolerable daily intake 50 µg per kg of body weight, expressed as DEHP equivalents
values.note: EFSA set the group value in December 2019 for the phthalates that share a common mechanism, the reduction of fetal testosterone. The individual values are 0.01 mg/kg of body weight per day for DBP, 0.5 for BBP, 0.05 for DEHP and 0.15 for DINP and DIDP; DIDP sits outside the group because its critical effect is on the liver.

values.label: DIDP
values.value: Tolerable daily intake 0.15 mg per kg of body weight
values.note: EFSA kept a separate value for di-isodecyl phthalate in December 2019: its critical effect is on the liver, so it sits outside the group value set for the phthalates that reduce fetal testosterone.
